chunks: And Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Saymari narrated, saying:

I entered upon Abu Ahmad Ubaidullah ibn Abdullah ibn Tahir, and before him was a note from Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which it was written: 'I prayed to Allah against this transgressor - meaning al-Musta'in - and He would seize him after three days.' So when the third day came, he was divested (of the caliphate), and what happened to him occurred until he was killed.

key_terms.رِقْعَةٌ: A note / a piece of paper
key_terms.نَازَلْتُ اللَّهَ: I prayed to Allah / I engaged Allah in a matter of prayer

ai.seo_question: What was the prediction of Imam Hasan al-Askari regarding the Caliph al-Musta'in?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the spiritual authority of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) during the Abbasid Caliphate, specifically his supplication (*du'a*) against the 'Taghut' Caliph al-Musta'in. The rapid fulfillment of this prediction—deposition on the third day and eventual death—serves as a key indicator of the Imam’s intercessory power and divine favor (*tawfiq*) amidst political turmoil. It underscores the Shia belief in the Imam’s active role in guiding historical events through divine decree.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 172 - Ali bin Muhammad bin Ziyad Saymoori said:

I came to Abu Ahmad Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Tahir; there was a letter of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) before him and it was written therein: I prayed to Almighty Allah against this transgressor [Mustaeen] and God’s fury would overtake him after three days. On the third day, Mustaeen was divested of Caliphate and killed.
